title: Deleting the index-1 rehearsal mint removed the only executable proof that Uniboost.setNudgeStreamer landed on indices 1/2/3; the local run now exits 0 with all three dispatchers unmintable
description: _finalizeUniboost writes dispatcher.setNudgeStreamer(address(nudgeStreamer)) with no read-back require, unlike the SYA idiom at :1267. At 9563c68 the omission was caught transitively by story-079's _accrueIndex1MintDebt mint; e6eded0 deleted it (NFTMinterV2.mint 10 -> 0).
impact: A mainnet operator relying on the local mirror to catch a missed setNudgeStreamer gets a green run. On mainnet that misconfiguration reverts every mint on indices 1/2/3 ('Uniboost: nudgeStreamer unset', Uniboost.sol:248). Local-only blast radius, hence Low; Medium was considered because the class is exactly what the mainnet cutover fears, and consistency with ledger eda17642 (Low) decided it.
evidence: Four-run controlled experiment, spot-reproduced by the orchestrator: artifacts/s3-control-sim.log CONTROL_EXIT=0; artifacts/s3-broken-sim.log BROKEN_EXIT=0 with wiring removed; artifacts/s3-broken-with-mintprobe.log BROKEN_WITH_PROBE_EXIT=1 'Error: script failed: Uniboost: nudgeStreamer unset'; artifacts/s3-pristine-with-mintprobe.log PRISTINE_WITH_PROBE_EXIT=0. Break patch artifacts/s3-break-patch.diff is a single-line comment-out at :1736.
recommendation: Add require(dispatcher.nudgeStreamer() == address(nudgeStreamer), "<label>: nudgeStreamer not wired") as the last line of _finalizeUniboost, matching the SYA idiom at :1267. Cheaper than restoring the mint and closes the same gap.

title: The three UniboostStakerV2 instances are published to the UI with zero stake and a zero phUSD reward budget: topUp and depositFor were the only producers and _deployUniboostStaker never tops up
description: topUp (6 -> 0) and depositFor(address,uint256) (9 -> 0) vanished with the V1 staker rehearsal. All three stakers end at totalStaked=0, phUSD.balanceOf=0, rewardBudget=0, rewardRate=0, with depletionWindowMonths=12.
impact: Not bricking - setDepletionWindow(12) with a zero budget is inert (rate 0, windowEnd = now+365d, verified) and the state self-heals on the first hook.pull(). But the chain the UI is tested against ships three reward-bearing contracts that emit nothing, which is not the 'fully working' end state the script claims.
recommendation: Either call staker.topUp(REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET) once per staker inside _deployUniboostStaker (the constant already existed at 9563c68), or restore the single index-1 mint so hook.pull() funds them organically. Assert rewardRate > 0 afterwards so a future removal fails loudly.

title: REGRESSION: story-079's Phase 7.6 dispatcher-swap rehearsal (ledger eda17642, fix-pending) was deleted, returning setDispatcher / replaceDispatcher / pull / NFT-mint to zero executions
description: Ledger eda17642828a6dd3 was accepted as fix-pending and fixed by story-079's _rehearseDispatcherSwap. e6eded0 deletes the helper, leaving only _pinNudgeRatchetStaticClaims (story-079 checklist item 540 - 1 of 6 L-01 items).
impact: The one cutover ordering whose wrong direction is silent rather than loud is again never executed locally. A fix-pending entry regressing is ranked immediately below an incomplete fix.
evidence: pull 1->0, setDispatcher 1->0, replaceDispatcher 1->0, mint(uint256,address) 10->0 (artifacts/s1-selector-counts-head.log, s1-selector-counts-baseline.log, s1-baseline-targets.log); deleted helper preserved at artifacts/s3-deleted-rehearsal.txt
recommendation: Reopen eda17642 as a regression rather than proposing it fixed. If the swap rehearsal is genuinely obsolete, that decision needs a story that says so and supersedes story-079's items 536-541 explicitly - not an untagged deletion.

title: Two of the deletions are justified by in-source claims about live mainnet state that a mainnet fork disproves
description: (a) The comment replacing the deleted PhlimboEA key states V2 'still exists on mainnet wound down, mint-revoked and NOT paused so a late staker can still exit'. Fork @25949772: paused() == true. The same claim is repeated in AddressLoader.sol:86-92. (b) DeployMocks.s.sol:2258-2263 justifies the new PhlimboV3 literal 604800 as 'the ones V2 carried and V3 inherited at the mainnet cutover'; mainnet V2 and V3 both read 2592000.
impact: No value at risk today (V2 holds totalStaked 0 and zero balances). The defect is that two irreversible edits rest on assertions about mainnet that were never checked, and the 604800 literal now pins the local depletion window 4.29x faster than mainnet's with no live read left to correct it.
evidence: artifacts/s5-mainnet-phlimboea.log (spot-reproduced by orchestrator: paused()=true, totalStaked()=0, depletionDuration()=2592000, phUSD and USDC balanceOf = 0); artifacts/s4-mainnet-v3-config.log; artifacts/s4-mainnet-phase4e.log (DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol:1752 reads both args live off V2)
recommendation: Correct both comments against the chain. For the depletion window either use 2592000 to mirror mainnet or state the 7-day value as a deliberate local divergence with a reason, the way LOCAL_STREAM_DURATION and LOCAL_PROMO_DURATION already do.

title: A live mainnet contract's only published resolution path was deleted to satisfy an interface constraint that is unenforced and already violated by three other keys
description: The stated reason for deleting the PhlimboEA key is that it 'left the generated ContractAddresses interface this file must satisfy'. That constraint is a console.error string in generate-ts-addresses.js:81, not a check - nothing runs tsc. And it is already violated: the file carries 3 keys the interface does not (BurnerEYE/BurnerSCX/BurnerFlax, :108-110), retained since story 070 for exactly the historical-reference reason PhlimboEA was denied.
impact: Aggravates open ledger F-04 (ee5aae66). An inconsistently-applied, unenforceable rule is now the precedent for removing live mainnet addresses from the only hand-maintained address book.
evidence: artifacts/ledger-recheck-static.log - interface 55 keys, mainnet-addresses.ts 58, 0 missing, 3 extra; artifacts/s5-addressbook-diff.log
recommendation: Restore the PhlimboEA key as a commented historical entry alongside the Burner precedent, or delete the three Burner keys so the rule is real. Then make the guard executable (a tsc --noEmit over server/deployments/, or a node key-set diff wired into generate:ts-anvil) - which also closes F-04.

title: Stale references to the deleted Phase 7.4 survive in the retained StableStaker cutover and in the toggle documentation
description: DeployMocks.s.sol:408 tells the reader not to scroll 'to Phase 7.4' for the toggle leg (the arming now happens in Phase 3, inside _deployPhlimboV3). DeployMocks.s.sol:2031, inside the RETAINED story-080 cutover, justifies revoking StableStakerV1's mint grant as mirroring 'PhlimboV2's treatment in the Phase 7.4 cutover' - a comparator that no longer exists. Ledger L-06 (08adbb69) rests on the same vanished landmark.
impact: QA. The :2031 instance is the one that matters: it is the load-bearing justification for a still-live revoke inside the surviving exception, and a future reader cannot verify it.
recommendation: Repoint :2031 at _deployPhlimboV3:2287-2321, which is the live in-file precedent for both the mint grant and the role stand-down, and drop the Phase 7.4 pointer at :408. When re-triaging L-06, restate its basis on _deployPhlimboV3:2314-2321 - the slimmed code now demonstrates the correct pattern one screen away from the place that omits it.

title: DepositView.sol and DepositPageView.sol are now first-party in-scope contracts with zero deployers, retained only as wagmi ABIs and a revival guard
description: Both are typed against the V1/V2-shaped IPhlimbo whose 3-tuple userInfo silently mis-decodes PhlimboV3's 4-tuple rather than reverting. No script deploys them any more; their ABIs remain in wagmi.config.ts and their names remain in extract-addresses.js DROPPED_CONTRACT_NAMES as a revival guard.
impact: QA. Live, published ABIs for contracts that cannot be safely pointed at the only phlimbo generation that exists, with nothing in the build preventing a consumer from wiring one up.
recommendation: Delete both sources and their wagmi entries, or add a compile-time impossibility (retype against IPhlimboV3, which will not compile against the 3-tuple). Keeping the extract-addresses.js guard entries is correct either way and should be noted as deliberate.

title: F-01: e6eded0 is untagged, has no story, and silently unwinds 5 of the 6 L-01 acceptance criteria of story-079, which sits in complete/
description: An exhaustive glob of the whole ~/code/product-owner/stories/phStaging2 tree (all states, all sprint folders, 82 files) tops out at story 081; a full-tree grep for slim/trim/retire-the-rehearsal/remove-old-cutover returns zero hits. No story authorises this commit. Story 079 checklist items 536-541 mandate the Phase 7.6 rehearsal; e6eded0 deletes it, satisfying only item 540 (the static index-7 claims). Items 533-535 (L-03 toggle) and 542 (L-04 sweep) are retained intact - the reversal is precisely and only story-079's L-01 half.
impact: A completed story's remediation was reverted with no superseding decision record, and the audit finding it closed (ledger eda17642, fix-pending) is live again with nothing in the tree explaining why. The three deleted rehearsals may well be genuinely obsolete - the argument in the source comments is coherent - but that judgement is unreviewable as filed.
evidence: artifacts/s3-deleted-rehearsal.txt, s1-selector-counts-head.log, s1-selector-counts-baseline.log, ledger-entries.log; closure-manifest.json storyDocs[0]
recommendation: Write the story. It needs to name story-079 items 536-541 and story-073's staker rehearsal as deliberately superseded, record the retained-exceptions rule and its two members, and carry the compensating assertions (the setNudgeStreamer read-back and a non-zero staker budget) so the assertion coverage the mint used to provide is not simply lost.
